correctness.rationale: Each closed neighborhood is a tetrahedron A_v={v-1,v,v+1,v+n}. In a cubic Möbius ladder n>=4, triangle T_v={v-1,v+1,v+n} is unique to A_v and then rim diagonal d_v={v-1,v+1} is unique to the remaining rim triangle R_v; 2n+2n free collapses leave exactly four boundary triangles on each square {i,i+1,i+n,i+n+1}. Adjacent boundaries intersect in one rung and nonadjacent ones are disjoint. Graph F consisting of all rungs plus one rim path has one cycle and meets each 2-sphere in a contractible 3-edge path, giving the integral wedge, not only Betti ranks. Explicit orientation z_i=∂[i,i+n,i+1,i+n+1] shows rotation z_i=z_(i+1), reflection z_i=z_(-i-1), while rim/rung relation gives reflection sign on unique H1 loop. Independently enumerated and free-face-checked n=4,5,6,7,8,10; initial f=(2n,7n,8n,2n), residual=(2n,5n,4n). Sources: Pinned source RESULT.md Git blob c422d3ee69927f497a09a8deff46139ab5990735, Steps 1-6, explicit z_i and gamma.; Independently checked free cofaces and residual geometric face sets at n=4,5,6,7,8,10; exact all-n proof is the adjacency/necklace argument.

final_claim: For n>=4, the closed-neighborhood complex of the Möbius ladder M_(2n) collapses in 4n free pairs onto n tetrahedral-boundary spheres glued in a cycle, giving S^1 wedge n S^2 and integral dihedral actions: rotation fixes H1 and cyclically permutes H2 basis, reflection negates H1 and permutes H2 unsigned.
limitations: n>=4 only; n=3 exceptional K_(3,3); closed neighborhoods, not OPEN Lovász neighborhoods.
The collapse is nonequivariant; dihedral statements are solely on integral homology, not an equivariant wedge decomposition.
